commit.message:
fix(resume): stoppable inline resume, spawn budget kept, nested max_turns

Follow-ups from review of d7c9ec0 (#368). The inline resume never installed
a fresh AbortController, so a stop could not reach it; it now arms one like
the detached path and stops up front on an already-cancelled call. One
settleOutcome helper serves spawn and both resume paths. A resume falls
back to the limit its spawn was given before the default, nested resumes
forward max_turns, and a foreground resume shows its own turn counter and
tool activity in the widget.

fix(resume): enforce max_turns and count turns on resumed agents

Fixes #368.

The steer → grace → abort machine lived only in runAgent, so a resumed
run had no turn limit and its widget counter never left turn 1. The
turn_end observer is now shared by runAgent and resumeAgent; a resume
resolves its limit like a spawn (explicit, else the agent's max_turns,
else the default) and counts from the resume prompt. AgentManager maps
the outcome with the spawn path's precedence, so a resumed run can end
steered or aborted, and both Agent-tool resume branches pass the limit
and a turn counter through. Nested and workflow resumes inherit the
limit via the record's type.

feat(rpc): add subagents:rpc:steer for cross-extension callers (#292)

* feat(rpc): add subagents:rpc:steer for cross-extension callers

An extension that spawns an agent over the bus and then learns something
that agent needs mid-run had no way to hand it over: it could spawn a
duplicate agent for the same work or drop the fact. The new channel is the
bus-side half of steer_subagent: id only, the same top-level ownership guard
as stop, 'Agent is not running' once the record has settled, and a message
sent before the session exists is flushed on creation. Outside the ping
version handshake like consume.

* fix(rpc): emit subagents:steered from the steer channel

The tool and @handle paths emit it; the bus path went through
manager.steer, which never does, so observers missed every bus steer.
Also covers consume and steer in the lifecycle-gating channel list,
splits the message-validation test, and updates stale comments and docs.

* fix(agents): emit subagents:steered from AgentManager.steer

The viewer and fleet-list steers never emitted it, and the @handle and
RPC paths each emitted by hand. One onSteered callback on the manager
now covers every path except the steer_subagent tool. Also dedupes the
stop/steer ownership guard and corrects the RPC docs.

* docs: name steer in the ownership section, fix changelog order

Also corrects the onSteered comments to cover the nested steer tool
and the stale rationale in the RPC gating test.

---------

Co-authored-by: tintinweb <tintinweb@oststrom.com>

commit.message: docs(changelog): add subagents:usage and subagents:disposed entry (#377)

feat(usage): per-message subagents:usage event for every agent, and subagents:disposed at shutdown (#377)

* feat(usage): emit subagents:usage per assistant message, for every agent

One event per message of spend, from the manager hook every agent's usage
already passes through: top-level, nested and workflow children alike, live
while the agent runs. Carries type, model, effective thinking level, depth,
parentAgentId, workflowId and the message's spend as a pi Usage. Ungated by
reportUsage. Lets another extension keep its own ledger, e.g. a footer that
breaks subagent cost down by type and thinking level.

* feat(usage): requestedThinking on subagents:usage, and subagents:disposed at shutdown

subagents:usage now carries requestedThinking when an agent did not get the
level it asked for (clamped to the model, or outranked by an agent file).

subagents:disposed fires at the end of session_shutdown, after every agent is
stopped and every child session has shut down. A ledger that flushes in its
own session_shutdown can run before the agents are aborted and miss their last
messages; this is the point after which a final flush is complete.

* fix(events): omit unknown usage keys, document sync disposed flush, pin ordering and clamp in tests

---------

Co-authored-by: tintinweb <tintinweb@oststrom.com>

commit.message: update agents.md
chore(release): 0.22.0

fix: dispose the activation-owned widget and group joins on shutdown (#256) (#316)

`session_shutdown` released the fleet, scheduler, manager, and pending nudges,
but skipped two resources created by the same activation: the AgentWidget (an
80ms render interval plus registered UI state) and the GroupJoinManager (pending
30s group timeouts). The Node process survives reload and session replacement,
so those timers can retain the old activation and fire its callbacks into the
fresh session's UI and group state — repeated reloads accumulate them.

Refresh of #316 onto 0.21.0: the batch-debounce half of that change is obsolete
now that background completions are delivered through the outbox at the parent's
next boundary, so this keeps only the widget and group-join disposal.
`session_before_switch` still deliberately keeps both: a vetoed switch continues
the session, where the live UI and group state must survive.

commit.message:
feat(agents): discover subagents and workflows declared by installed pi packages (#262)

* feat(agents): discover subagents and workflows declared by installed pi packages

* fix(agents): close package-discovery gaps found in review, and document the feature

Follow-up to the feature commit; all of it is still unreleased.

- package-resources.ts held two literal NUL bytes as cache-key separators, so
  the whole module read as binary and ripgrep silently skipped it.
- Eject dropped `ext:` tool selectors, `persist_session` and `session_dir` from
  a package agent. The ejected copy shadows the package file, so the running
  agent silently lost tools. Only reachable since package agents became
  ejectable — a built-in default carries none of those fields.
- `strictAgentFiles` aborted activation over an unparseable `.md` inside an
  installed package. Strict mode now covers only files the user owns.
- `!` manifest exclusions were inert against a file inside an included
  directory, which is the only form that does anything. Now applied at load
  time, for agents and workflows.
- `"packageAgents": "my-pkg"` was dropped as malformed and fell back to the
  `true` default, silently admitting every package. Read as a one-entry list.
- A symlinked `agents/` pointing out of the package passed the root check.
  Containment now compares canonical paths.
- A workflow declared as a single file promoted its parent directory to a
  name-resolution root, exposing scripts the package never declared. Declared
  files now resolve through an exact name map.
- Project trust is seeded at activation from pi's saved decision. The Agent
  tool description is built before `session_start`, so a package named in a
  committed `.pi/settings.json` was dispatchable but never advertised to the
  model — the team-distribution case from #109.
- Carry the manifest declaration on PiPackage instead of re-reading it.

Adds docs/packages.md and trims the README section to a summary that links it.

* doc

* feat(agents): name the package a subagent came from in /agents

The `▪` package badge shipped without a legend key, so a package agent
rendered a glyph nothing on screen explained — and the badge says only
that *some* package won, not which one, which is also the string a user
needs for a `packageAgents` allowlist.

- package-resources: the memoized scan now records each admitted
  package's normalized root and display name, longest root first, so a
  package nested in another's node_modules claims its own files. New
  `packageNameForPath()` traces a loaded `sourcePath` back to it. No
  extra fs work; inherits the existing gate/trust keying and cache
  invalidation.
- agent-source-badge (new): `sourceIndicator`/`sourceLegend`/
  `rowDescription`, extracted from the `/agents` closure the way
  agent-file-toggle.ts was, since `registerCommand` is mocked in every
  wiring test. The legend is now derived from the badges actually on
  screen, so a glyph can't ship without its key again — and a roster
  whose only custom agent is disabled no longer renders `✕•` with no
  key, nor a global-only roster a `•` that appears nowhere.
- /agents: a package row prefixes the highlighted-row description with
  the full `@scope/name`; the detail menu is titled `<name> — <package>`.
  No new column, row, or grouping.

* fixup! feat(agents): discover subagents and workflows declared by installed pi packages

* test(agents): cover the meta check on a single-file package workflow

* update changelog

commit.message:
feat: deliver background completions at the parent's next boundary, as in Claude Code (#388)

* feat: deliver background completions at the parent's next boundary

Hold completion notifications while the parent runs and send what
is pending as one steer message at turn_end, or after a 200 ms hold
when it is idle, as Claude Code does. No result waits for its
siblings: smart (and async) no longer group, and group mode batches
by parent turn instead of a 100 ms spawn window. An aborted turn's
notifications go out with the next prompt.

* fix: deliver a completion pending at ESC once the run ends, as in CC

* fix: report a lone `group` spawn as a single completion

registerTurnGroup registered any non-empty turn batch, so a turn with
one `group` spawn got "Background agent group completed: 1 agent(s)"
without the transcript footer. Only batches of two or more form a group
now, as on master.

* update tests: live

* fix: build a completion notification when the agent finishes

The outbox built each notification at send time from the live record,
so an agent resumed before the parent's boundary was reported as
running with no output, or with the inline resume's result, and a
result read before the resume came back as a notification.

Build at completion and cancel by id when the result is read
(get_subagent_result, rpc consume); a newer completion of the same
agent replaces its pending one, as scheduleNudge did. Group members
cancel one at a time.

* remove dead code
update docs to not cite lines but symbols

* fix: deliver a completion that lands while the parent's run is settling

* update changelog

commit.message:
chore(deps): bump vitest to 4.1.11 and source-map-js to 1.2.2

Resolves npm audit advisories GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9 (@vitest/mocker
redirect path traversal) and GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q (source-map-js
indexed-map DoS). @vitest/coverage-istanbul pins its vitest peer
exactly, so both move to ^4.1.11 together; the rest of the lockfile
churn is vitest's dev-only transitive tree (vite 8.3.4, rolldown 1.2.13).

chore(release): 0.21.0
test: pin steer-scheduling e2e to faux under PI_E2E_LIVE

fix: steer background completion notifications to a busy parent (#387)

* fix: steer background completion notifications

* test: initialize blocking tool control safely

* test: allow loaded scheduling startup

* fix: steer workflow completions, align tests and docs with master

- Workflow completions also use deliverAs "steer", so they arrive
  at the same point as agent completions.
- The wiring test mocks registerEntryRenderer, registerFlag and
  getFlag. In the grouped test, runs settle after their spawns
  return, as real runs do.
- The e2e test finds the parent with getCurrentTools(context.messages).
  The idle-parent test is dropped: it called pi's sendCustomMessage
  directly and never exercised the extension.
- README and docs/rpc.md describe Claude Code's timing: a busy parent
  gets the notification after its current tool batch, and an idle
  parent gets a new turn.

* docs: drop stale follow-up wording from notification comments

* docs(changelog): credit #387 for steered completion notifications

commit.message:
feat(fleet): send a running foreground agent to the background with ctrl+b (#261)

* feat(fleet): send a live foreground agent to the background with `b` (#233)

* feat(fleet): send a running foreground agent to the background

Press ctrl+b while a foreground Agent call runs to hand it to the
background, as in Claude Code. The same run keeps going (same session,
in-flight turn, transcript and worktree). The blocked call returns the
result a run_in_background spawn gets. Completion arrives as the normal
background notification, naming the original tool call.

- ctrl+b hands off every running foreground Agent call at once. It is
  claimed only while one is running and the prompt editor has focus;
  key releases are ignored. A dim "(ctrl+b to run in background)" hint
  appears after 2s, on one row per batch.
- `b` in the conversation viewer (FleetView, /agents) hands off just
  that agent.
- AgentManager.sendToBackground moves the slot from the foreground
  pool to the background pool and removes the caller's parent-abort
  listener, so Esc no longer reaches the run. It refuses nested,
  workflow, queued and resumed runs.
- Only the Agent tool registers a call that can be handed off, so the
  agent generator and workflow agents are never offered it.
- A handoff emits subagents:created with isBackground: true, as a
  detached resume does.
- Fix forwardAbortSignal ignoring a parent signal that was already
  aborted before the child session existed.

Supersedes #233.

* update readme/changelog. add test

* fix(runner): don't prompt a child whose signal already fired

A pre-aborted signal never fires addEventListener, and pi's
session.abort() is a no-op until a run is active, so the guard in
forwardAbortSignal did nothing: the child was prompted and ran to
completion with its parent gone. runAgent and resumeAgent now skip
session.prompt() when the signal has already fired.

Tests now assert prompt is never called (the old ones only checked
call order on a mock). Merge the two #261 CHANGELOG bullets into one.

feat(ui): support Pi's fullscreen TUI mode (#357)

* feat(ui)!: add fullscreen subagent conversation observer

Keep the regular floating viewer and use a full-terminal observer only with the active fullscreen renderer. Add isolated mouse scrolling, native scrollbar preferences, and a pinned new-message indicator.

Adapt mention cloning and scripted provider tests to the Pi APIs required by the observer.

BREAKING CHANGE: Requires Pi 0.87.1 or newer.

* fix(ui): preserve Pi 0.84 compatibility and narrow fullscreen scope

Gate the fullscreen observer on host and component mouse capabilities. Keep the original regular viewer scroll behavior and fall back on older hosts.

Restore upstream dependency versions, CI, session cloning, and unrelated tests. Limit the PR to the viewer, its entry points, focused tests, and documentation.

---------

commit.message:
fix: load pi's built-in extensions in subagents, scope and trust them (#386)

* fix: load pi's built-in extensions in subagent sessions

A subagent's resource loader is built in agent-runner rather than by pi's CLI,
so it started with none of pi's built-in extensions. A `builtin:<name>` entry in
an agent's `extensions:` therefore resolved to nothing and the extension was
silently dropped, putting pi's built-in MCP, codemode, and tool search out of
reach for every subagent.

Forward the host's factories through the loader's `extensionFactories` option.
The names are read at runtime and guarded, so a pi that exports none of them
keeps the previous behavior.

* fix: load pi's built-in extensions in subagents, scope and trust them

Forward codemode, tool-search and MCP to the child loader as `builtin:`
resources, so subagents get them as the main session does; `--no-mcp`
and `exclude_extensions: builtin:mcp` opt out.

- Subagents inherit the parent's project trust; a spawn into another
  directory reports that directory untrusted, so its `.pi/mcp.json`
  never runs.
- Activate only tools pi would declare (exposure, defaultActive).
- Scope-check calls made through ctx.executeTool via an inline
  tool_call gate.

Supersedes #379 and #383 (thanks @misbahulard). Partly addresses #370.

* fix: honour -ne for pi's built-ins in subagents; document naming the MCP bridge under ext:

---------

commit.message:
fix: apply an agent file's `isolation` on mention and RPC spawns

The manager now resolves the file's `isolation:` itself, so direct-mode
and fallback @handle mentions, reclaimed agents and RPC spawns honour
`worktree` and `off`, and the widget tags every worktree agent.
Workflow agent() keeps Claude Code's behaviour: only the script's
option decides.

fix: apply an agent file's `isolated` on every spawn path

runAgent read only `options.isolated`, so the agent file's value held
only where the caller resolved it first (Agent tool, nested tools,
scheduler, and workflows since #339). `@handle` mentions and RPC or
registry spawns that omitted it loaded every host extension for an
`isolated: true` agent.

The runner now resolves `agentConfig?.isolated ?? options.isolated`:
the agent file wins, and the caller decides only when the file leaves it
unset, matching README's "Frontmatter is authoritative". An RPC caller's
explicit `isolated: false` no longer overrides a file's `true`.

fix: honour an agent's `isolated` in SubagentWorkflow spawns (#339)

The Agent tool resolves `isolated` off the agent definition and passes it to
the manager as a spawn option. The workflow host never did, so an agent file's
`isolated: true` was silently dropped for every child a script spawned.

That inverts what the flag is for. `isolated` exists to draw a hermetic
boundary — no extensions, no skills, no ext: selectors — and agents given it
are typically the read-only ones. Dropped, they loaded the full host extension
set and picked up its tools.

Observed by asking the same read-only `scout` definition to enumerate its
tools down both paths: via SubagentWorkflow it listed web_search, mcpScript
and six mcp__* tools; via Agent it correctly had none of them. The builtin
allowlist was applied in both cases, so only the extension half leaked.

The config is already resolved here for the model-precedence logic, so this
just forwards it.

Co-authored-by: Ajay Krishnan <ajaynomics@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message: test: cover queued foreground startup failure; fix stale isError comments
fix(ui): accept any EditorComponent as the focused prompt editor (#374)
fix(ui): add bottom spacer below FleetView list (#351)
chore: release v0.20.0

fix: support pi 1.1.0 (#384)

pi 0.86/0.87 moved the system prompt and history into the session
transcript.

- mention clone: seed it via SessionManager.inMemory(entries) and a
  resource-loader prompt override instead of writing agent state
  (systemPrompt is a read-only getter; every mention fell back)
- output file: start after the first user message and skip system
  messages (prompt was written twice, system messages as toolResult)
- typebox becomes a "*" peer; drop @sinclair/typebox from deps
  (silences pi's host-provided dependency warning)
- peer floor, dev pin and CI floor job move to pi 1.1.0
- tests read tools/prompt via getCurrentTools/getCurrentSystemPrompt

Closes #365 (diagnosis and approach thanks @jeremy7687)
Closes #358, closes #362, closes #366, closes #382

Supersedes #359 (first fix, thanks @Arteiimis), #360, #364, #367,
than declared, since src/ no longer imports it.
